title: Enhanced Portfolio Optimization (EPO)
text: Enhanced Portfolio Optimization (EPO) method, described Pedersen, Babu, Levine (2021), addresses long-standing puzzle quantitative finance: standard mean-variance optimization (MVO) highest possible Sharpe ratio theory, yet performs poorly --sample many investors abandon optimization altogether favor naive rules 1/N portfolio. Pedersen, Babu, Levine trace failure specific set “problem portfolios.” Decomposing correlation matrix principal components (long-short portfolios uncorrelated ranked variance), show least important components ones wreck MVO: portfolios lowest ex-ante risk, estimation error tends underestimate true volatility, noise expected-return estimates large relative low risk. optimizer sees noise-driven portfolios offering deceptively high Sharpe ratios consequently takes large, highly-leveraged bets — bets perform poorly --sample. fix proposed paper, “Simple EPO”, small change outsized effect: shrink -diagonal correlations toward zero optimizing. Correlation shrinkage raises estimated volatility exactly problem portfolios (unimportant principal components), turn shrinks inflated Sharpe ratios back toward levels actually observed --sample. single adjustment stabilizes MVO , empirically, produces large improvements realized Sharpe ratio statistically significant alpha relative market, 1/N, standard factor benchmarks. One shrinkage parameter, \(w \[0, 1]\), controls whole procedure: \(w = 0\) recovers standard MVO (shrinkage). \(w = 1\) sets correlations zero, (scaling) equivalent optimizing . \(w \(0, 1)\) interpolates two, paper finds fairly large shrinkage (around 75% empirical applications) tends work well — correlation shrinkage corrects noise risk model expected-return estimates, just former. practice \(w\) chosen empirically (e.g., --sample, picking value maximized realized Sharpe ratio using past data). package also implements “Anchored EPO”, lets investor keep optimized portfolio close reference benchmark portfolio (“anchor”) — example strategic asset allocation, benchmark index, 1/N portfolio. \(w = 0\) yields standard MVO, \(w = 1\) collapses solution onto anchor, intermediate values produce Black-Litterman-style portfolios \(w\) plays role investor’s confidence anchor relative signal. Unlike Black-Litterman, however, anchor need market portfolio, makes Anchored EPO considerably general. Beyond empirical performance, one paper’s central contributions theoretical: shows EPO solution nests standard MVO, reverse-MVO, Black-Litterman model, robust optimization ellipsoidal uncertainty set expected returns, ridge-regression-style regularization special cases — unifying several strands portfolio-optimization literature single, transparent shrinkage parameter.

title: Enhanced Portfolio Optimization (EPO)
code: library(epo)  x <- diff(log(EuStockMarkets)) # stock returns s <- colMeans(x) # it could be any signal   ################## ### The Simple EPO ##################  # Traditional Mean-Variance Analysis epo(x = x, signal = s, lambda = 10, method = "simple", w = 0) #> [1]  0.1914569  0.9894828 -0.3681779  0.1872382  # 100% Shrinkage epo(x = x, signal = s, lambda = 10, method = "simple", w = 1) #> [1] 0.2352863 0.3659986 0.1375249 0.2611902  # 50% Classical MVO and 50% Shrinkage epo(x = x, signal = s, lambda = 10, method = "simple", w = 0.5) #> [1]  0.223281853  0.564005906 -0.009868083  0.222580324  #################### ### The Anchored EPO  ####################  benchmark <- rep(0.25, 4) # 1/N Portfolio  # Traditional Mean-Variance Analysis epo(x = x, signal = s, lambda = 10, method = "anchored", w = 0.0, anchor = benchmark) #> [1]  0.1914569  0.9894828 -0.3681779  0.1872382  # 100% on the Anchor portfolio epo(x = x, signal = s, lambda = 10, method = "anchored", w = 1.0, anchor = benchmark) #> [1] 0.25 0.25 0.25 0.25  # 50% on Mean-Variance Analysis and 50% on the Anchor Portfolio epo(x = x, signal = s, lambda = 10, method = "anchored", w = 0.5, anchor = benchmark) #> [1] 0.2374674 0.4557503 0.1004711 0.2063111

title: Enhanced Portfolio Optimization (EPO) — epo
text: x data-set asset returns. tibble, xts matrix. signal double vector investor's beliefs expected returns (signals, forecasts) asset x. lambda double investor's (absolute) risk-aversion coefficient, paper's notation. method = "simple", resulting portfolio's Sharpe ratio depend lambda, positive value works normalize = TRUE. method = "anchored" endogenous = TRUE, argument ignored risk-aversion coefficient calibrated internally. method character. One : "simple" "anchored". w double 0 1. EPO shrinkage parameter: 0 yields standard mean-variance optimization (shrinkage) 1 yields maximum shrinkage (anchor portfolio, method = "anchored", unoptimized portfolio, method = "simple"). practice, w often chosen empirically, e.g. picking value maximized realized Sharpe ratio using past (--sample) data. anchor double vector anchor (benchmark) portfolio allocation deviate much (e.g. strategic asset allocation, market-cap benchmark, 1/N portfolio). used method = "anchored". normalize boolean indicating whether allocation normalized sum 1 (full-investment constraint). default normalize = TRUE. endogenous boolean indicating whether risk-aversion parameter calibrated endogenously anchor signal (paper's footnote 13), rather taken lambda. used method = "anchored". default endogenous = TRUE.

title: Enhanced Portfolio Optimization (EPO) — epo
text: Standard mean-variance optimization (MVO) highly sensitive estimation error correlation matrix expected returns. error concentrated least important principal components correlation matrix ("problem portfolios"), whose risk tends underestimated whose expected return tends overestimated. EPO fixes shrinking -diagonal correlations toward zero factor w running MVO, increases estimated volatility (lowers implied Sharpe ratio) exactly problem portfolios. Two flavors EPO implemented, governed single shrinkage parameter, w, 0 (shrinkage, .e. standard MVO) 1 (maximum shrinkage): method = "simple" implements "Simple EPO" (paper's equation 16). allocation given \(x = \frac{1}{\lambda} \Sigma_w^{-1} s\), \(\Sigma_w\) variance-covariance matrix rebuilt shrunk correlation matrix \(\Omega_w = (1 - w) \Omega + w \). w = 1 correlations set zero, equivalent (scaling) optimizing . method = "anchored" implements "Anchored EPO" (paper's equation 17), pulls solution toward reference/benchmark portfolio, anchor. w = 0 solution standard MVO; w = 1 solution collapses onto anchor; values produce Black-Litterman-style portfolios w controls confidence placed anchor relative signal. Unlike Black-Litterman, anchor need market portfolio.
